name: smol-toml
license_evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/smol-toml/1.9.1 (license BSD-3-Clause; LICENSE file and SPDX headers in dist/)
input_api: parse(text, { integersAsBigInt: true }) on local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 text; the typed tree walks the returned TomlTable (BigInt integers, Number floats, TomlDate date-times)
scope: One TOML document from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 (BOM kept) and passed once to parse(text, { integersAsBigInt: true }). Only the two valid TOML 1.0.0 controls were run
family_note: smol-toml 1.9.1 has no runtime dependencies. dist/parse.js runs its own document loop over the text (table headers, arrays of tables, key/value lines) and dist/struct.js, dist/extract.js and dist/primitive.js parse keys, inline tables, arrays, strings, numbers and date-times by character scanning; dist/date.js holds TomlDate. It is not a wrapper over another parser. confbox 0.3.2 bundles a minified copy of this parser (dist/_chunks/libs/smol-toml.mjs), so confbox is in the smol-toml family, not a separate engine.
shared_family_statement: Own family. confbox's parseTOML is a bundled copy of smol-toml and would share this family.
verification_note: The README (tag v1.9.1) documents parse(toml, options) and the integersAsBigInt option ("parse integers as BigInt") and TomlDate with isDate()/isTime()/isLocal(). With integersAsBigInt: true every TOML integer is a BigInt and every float a Number, so integer 1000 and float 1e3 stay distinct; without the option both come back as the Number 1000. The adapter decodes the bytes with TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}), calls parse once and builds the typed tree from the returned values: BigInt -> integer, Number -> float (shortest round-trip digits written positionally), TomlDate isDate() -> date-local, isTime() -> time-local, isLocal() -> datetime-local, otherwise datetime as the UTC instant of Date.prototype.toISOString with the zero fraction trimmed. TomlDate keeps millisecond precision only; the controls need at most two fractional digits. Both controls match the expected typed trees exactly (data/javascript/toml/smol-toml-tree-verification.json). Only valid controls were run.

name: toml-eslint-parser
license_evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/toml-eslint-parser/1.0.3 (license MIT; LICENSE file in the tarball)
input_api: parseTOML(text, { tomlVersion: '1.0.0' }) on local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 text; the typed tree walks the returned TOML syntax tree (TOMLTable resolvedKey, TOMLKeyValue keys via getStaticTOMLValue, TOMLValue kind and value)
scope: One TOML document from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 (BOM kept) and passed once to parseTOML(text, { tomlVersion: '1.0.0' }); the typed tree is assembled from the syntax tree's resolved table keys, key paths and typed value nodes. Only the two valid TOML 1.0.0 controls were run
family: toml-eslint-parser (own code-point tokenizer and syntax-tree parser)
family_note: toml-eslint-parser 1.0.3 ships one bundled module, lib/index.mjs, holding its own code-point tokenizer (TOML 1.0/1.1 escapes, numbers, date-times), its own parser that builds ESLint-compatible TOML nodes and resolves table keys (resolvedKey with array-of-tables indices) and reports redefinitions, and getStaticTOMLValue. Its only dependency, eslint-visitor-keys 5.0.1, lists AST child keys and parses nothing. It does not call smol-toml, toml, @iarna/toml or any other TOML parser; it is a separate family from smol-toml.
shared_family_statement: Own family; no code shared with smol-toml or the confbox bundle.
verification_note: The README at gitHead 6008e35499342f1116262162d16dbcab0c84760c (the 1.0.3 tarball's gitHead) documents direct use: parseTOML(code) returns the AST and getStaticTOMLValue(ast) its static value, and parserOptions.tomlVersion selects 1.0.0 or 1.1.0 (default 1.1.0). getStaticTOMLValue alone returns plain Numbers and Dates, so integer 1000 and float 1e3 or a local date and an offset date-time cannot be told apart from it; the AST keeps them apart. The adapter decodes the bytes with TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}), calls parseTOML once with tomlVersion '1.0.0', and assembles the typed tree from the returned nodes: table paths from each TOMLTable's resolvedKey (array-of-tables entries carry numeric indices), key paths from getStaticTOMLValue(key), integers from the node's BigInt, floats from its Number (shortest round-trip digits written positionally), date-time kinds from the node kind with the Date's UTC fields (local kinds are stored as if UTC; the offset date-time Date is the instant). It never re-parses the text and does not read the raw datetime lexeme. Dates keep millisecond precision only; the controls need at most two fractional digits. Both controls match the expected typed trees exactly (data/javascript/toml/toml-eslint-parser-tree-verification.json). Only valid controls were run.

name: @ltd/j-toml
license_evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/@ltd/j-toml/1.38.0 (license LGPL-3.0; LICENSE file in the tarball)
input_api: TOML.parse[1.0](text, { joiner: '\n', bigint: true }) on local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 text; returns nested tables with BigInt integers, Number floats and OffsetDateTime/LocalDateTime/LocalDate/LocalTime objects
scope: One TOML document from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 (BOM kept) and passed once to TOML.parse[1.0](text, { joiner: '\n', bigint: true }); the typed tree is built from the returned tables, arrays and typed values. Offset date-times are observed with millisecond precision. Only the two valid TOML 1.0.0 controls were run
family_note: @ltd/j-toml 1.38.0 ships one implementation in index.js/index.mjs (the CommonJS and ES module builds of the same source): an iterator over source lines, its own TOML 1.0/0.5/0.4 key, table, array and value parser with version switches, its own string-escape, integer, float and date-time literal decoders, and its own OffsetDateTime, LocalDateTime, LocalDate and LocalTime classes. The package has no dependencies and calls no other TOML parser; it shares no code with smol-toml or toml-eslint-parser.
shared_family_statement: Own family; no code shared with smol-toml, toml-eslint-parser or toml-patch.
verification_note: The README in the 1.38.0 tarball documents TOML.parse(source[, options]) with options.joiner (the string that joins multi-line string lines; required when a document has multi-line strings) and options.bigint (true returns every integer as BigInt), and TOML.parse[1.0] to fix the specification version. With bigint: true, integers are BigInts and floats Numbers, so integer 1000 and float 1e3 stay distinct; offset date-times, local date-times, local dates and local times come back as distinct exported classes. The adapter decodes the bytes with TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}), calls TOML.parse[1.0] once with joiner '\n' and bigint true, and walks the result: offset date-times through the documented getUTC* getters (millisecond precision), local kinds through their toISOString, floats as shortest round-trip digits written positionally. Tables are instances of j-toml's internal null-prototype Table class. It never re-parses the text. Both controls match the expected typed trees exactly (data/javascript/toml/ltd-j-toml-tree-verification.json). Only valid controls were run.

name: @decimalturn/toml-patch
license_evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/@decimalturn/toml-patch/3.3.3 (license MIT; LICENSE file in the tarball)
input_api: parse(text, { integersAsBigInt: true }) on local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 text; returns plain objects with BigInt integers, Number floats and the exported OffsetDateTime/LocalDateTime/LocalDate/LocalTime Date subclasses
scope: One TOML document from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 (BOM kept) and passed once to parse(text, { integersAsBigInt: true }); the typed tree is built from the returned objects, arrays and typed values. Date-times are observed with millisecond precision. Only the two valid TOML 1.0.0 controls were run
family: toml-patch (Tim Hall's format-preserving TOML parser, maintained fork by DecimalTurn)
family_note: @decimalturn/toml-patch 3.3.3 is the maintained continuation of Tim Hall's toml-patch (npm toml-patch, 1,667 downloads in the same window, not selected): its own tokenizer, concrete/abstract syntax-tree parser that keeps comments and formatting, and AST-to-value conversion, published as one minified bundle dist/toml-patch.js. The package has no runtime dependencies and calls no other TOML parser; it shares no code with smol-toml, toml-eslint-parser or j-toml. @shopify/toml-patch, despite the name, is a WebAssembly build of Rust toml_edit (excluded).
shared_family_statement: Own family (toml-patch lineage); no code shared with smol-toml, toml-eslint-parser or j-toml.
verification_note: The package type declarations (dist/toml-patch.d.ts in the 3.3.3 tarball) document parse(value, options?) with ParseOptions.integersAsBigInt (true returns every integer as bigint; the default 'asNeeded' returns safe integers as Numbers, which would make integer 1000 and float 1e3 indistinguishable) and the exported Date subclasses LocalDate, LocalTime, LocalDateTime and OffsetDateTime. The adapter decodes the bytes with TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}), calls parse once with integersAsBigInt true, and walks the result: date kinds from the exported classes, their fields through Date.prototype.toISOString (millisecond precision; local kinds are stored in the Date's UTC fields, the offset date-time Date is the instant), floats as shortest round-trip digits written positionally. It never re-parses the text. The published bundle is minified into 83 long lines, so its line counts understate the code reached. Both controls match the expected typed trees exactly (data/javascript/toml/decimalturn-toml-patch-tree-verification.json). Only valid controls were run.

name: @effected/toml
license_evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/@effected/toml/0.20.0 (license MIT; LICENSE file in the tarball)
input_api: TomlVisitor.visit(text) on local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 text, collected with Effect.runSync(Stream.runCollect(...)); returns TableStart/ArrayTableStart events with resolved table paths and KeyValue events with resolved key paths and typed value nodes (TomlString, TomlInteger, TomlFloat, TomlBoolean, TomlDateTimeLiteral, TomlArray, TomlInlineTable)
scope: One TOML document from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 (BOM kept) and passed once to TomlVisitor.visit(text); the typed tree is assembled from the returned events' resolved paths and the parser's typed value nodes. Only the two valid TOML 1.0.0 controls were run
family: @effected/toml (spencerbeggs; own hand-written scanner, lossless syntax-tree parser and semantic analysis)
family_note: @effected/toml 0.20.0 (github.com/spencerbeggs/effected, packages/toml) is a from-scratch TOML 1.1.0 engine written against Effect: internal/scanner.js, internal/parser.js (a lossless linear syntax tree whose spans tile the source) and internal/semantic.js (table and key resolution, duplicate checks). Its README states it vendors no upstream code; its runtime dependencies are @effected/source (source-text positions) and the effect peer dependency. It calls no other TOML parser and shares no code with smol-toml, toml-eslint-parser, j-toml, toml-patch or toml.min. Its value-level Toml.parse returns safe integers as Numbers (so integer 1000 and float 1e3 would be the same Number); the documented TomlVisitor keeps the parser's TomlInteger and TomlFloat nodes apart.
shared_family_statement: Own family; no code shared with smol-toml, toml-eslint-parser, j-toml, toml-patch or toml.min.
verification_note: The 0.20.0 README and type declarations (index.d.ts) document TomlVisitor.visit(text): a Stream of TomlVisitorEvent in document order, with TableStart (path), ArrayTableStart (path and 0-based index), KeyValue (path including the final key, and the parsed TomlKeyValue node) and Comment events, failing with TomlParseError on lex, parse or semantic violations. The value-level Toml.parse is not used because it returns safe integers as plain Numbers. The adapter decodes the bytes with TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}), collects the events once with Effect.runSync(Stream.runCollect(...)) and assembles the tree: tables from the resolved paths (an array of tables resolves to the element its latest ArrayTableStart opened), scalars from the typed nodes, inline tables from their entries' decoded key paths, date-times formatted from the TomlOffsetDateTime/TomlLocalDateTime/TomlLocalDate/TomlLocalTime fields (offset date-times shifted by offsetMinutes to the UTC instant, nanosecond field kept). It never re-parses the text. Found by a targeted lookup of npm search hits without a lead decision. Both controls match the expected typed trees exactly (data/javascript/toml/effected-toml-tree-verification.json). Only valid controls were run.

name: @sgarciac/bombadil
license_evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/@sgarciac/bombadil/2.3.0 (license Artistic-2.0; LICENSE file in the tarball)
input_api: new TomlReader().readToml(text, true) on local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 text; result holds tables { type: 'table', content }, arrays and typed primitives { type, image, value } (README 'Full typing information'); errors holds lexer, parser and table-loading errors
scope: One TOML document from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 (BOM kept) and passed once to new TomlReader().readToml(text, true); the typed tree is built from the returned type tags and values. bombadil 2.3.0 implements TOML 0.5.0; the two controls lie in the subset 0.5.0 and 1.0.0 share. Date-times are observed with millisecond precision. Only the two valid TOML 1.0.0 controls were run
family: bombadil (sgarciac; own chevrotain TOML 0.5.0 lexer and grammar)
family_note: @sgarciac/bombadil 2.3.0 (2019, listed in the toml-lang wiki implementation list) defines its own TOML 0.5.0 tokens and grammar in lib/lexer.js and lib/parser.js and loads tables in lib/tables.js; the chevrotain 4.8.1 runtime executes those definitions (a generic parser-building library, like the ANTLR runtime under the Java tomlj path) and moment builds dates. It calls no other TOML parser and shares no code with smol-toml, toml-eslint-parser, j-toml, toml-patch, @effected/toml or toml.min.
shared_family_statement: Own family; no code shared with the other JavaScript TOML paths.
verification_note: The 2.3.0 README documents new bombadil.TomlReader, readToml(input) with result and errors, and the 'Full typing information' mode readToml(input, true), in which tables and primitives are objects with a type (table, atomicString, atomicInteger, atomicFloat, atomicBoolean, offsetDateTime, localDateTime, localDate, localTime), the toml image and the JavaScript value; without the flag integers and floats are both Numbers. The adapter decodes the bytes with TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}), calls readToml once with the flag, requires an empty errors list and walks the result using only type and value: Dates through Date.prototype.toISOString (local kinds are stored at UTC±00:00), integers only within the exact Number range, floats as shortest round-trip digits written positionally. The image strings are never read and the text is never re-parsed. bombadil targets TOML 0.5.0; both controls are inside the subset it shares with TOML 1.0.0. Found by a targeted lookup of npm search hits without a lead decision (also listed in the toml-lang wiki). Both controls match the expected typed trees exactly (data/javascript/toml/sgarciac-bombadil-tree-verification.json). Only valid controls were run.
